title: Jáuregui’s Arrest Does Not Close the CIA Case in Chihuahua; Morena Demands Broader Investigations
author: Darylh Rodríguez
content:
_This article by[Darylh Rodríguez](https://contralinea.com.mx/author/darylh/)
originally appeared in the [October 20, 2026 edition of
Contralínea](https://contralinea.com.mx/interno/semana/detencion-de-jauregui-
no-cierra-el-caso-de-la-cia-en-chihuahua-morena-exige-ampliar-
investigaciones/), a Mexican investigative journalism magazine._

The participation of agents of the United States Central Intelligence Agency
(**CIA**) in an anti-drug operation in Chihuahua, without authorization from
the federal government, constitutes a violation of national sovereignty,
charged **Morena**. The party held the PAN administration of **María Eugenia
Campos** politically responsible and demanded clarification of the
intervention of foreign personnel on Mexican territory. It also warned that
the investigations must not end with the arrest of former state prosecutor
**César Gustavo Jáuregui Moreno**.

Morena's national leader, Ariadna Montiel Reyes, considered that the
apprehension of the former official represents progress, but insisted that
**it is still necessary** **to locate Guillermo Arturo Zuany Portillo** , who
served as special prosecutor for Strategic Operations and Anti-Kidnapping when
the events took place.

"That one, who knows where he is, must also appear and be brought before the
authorities," said the Morena leader, who acknowledged the work of the head of
the Federal Attorney General's Office (FGR), **Ernestina Godoy Ramos** , in
the investigations.

Montiel maintained that **clarifying these events is fundamental to
guaranteeing respect for national sovereignty** , particularly given the
intervention of foreign agents in security operations without the
corresponding permits. In that context, she highlighted that the government of
President Claudia Sheinbaum and her security cabinet continue working to
combat crime and build peace.

The case gained prominence in April 2026, when a vehicle accident in the
Sierra Tarahumara caused the deaths of two U.S. citizens linked to the CIA and
two members of the Chihuahua State Attorney General's Office (FGE). The
victims were returning from the area where an operation against clandestine
synthetic drug laboratories had been carried out in El Pinal, in the
municipality of Morelos.

Initially, the state prosecutor's office maintained that the foreigners had
not taken part in the deployment and that they were in the region to provide
training on the handling of drones. However, federal investigations later
established that they took part in operational actions without the
corresponding authorization.

The FGR stated that local authorities allegedly exceeded their powers by
allowing foreign personnel to take part in tasks reserved for the Federation.
It also indicated that Jáuregui allegedly failed to inform federal
institutions in a timely manner about the activities carried out in El Pinal,
despite these being crimes within their jurisdiction.

On October 17, the Chihuahua Attorney General's Office arrested the former
official for his probable responsibility in state-level crimes, including
unlawful exercise of public service and coalition. Subsequently, federal
authorities executed an arrest warrant for acts possibly constituting treason
in matters of national security.

After appearing before a state judge, Jáuregui was placed in FGR custody and
transferred to Federal Social Rehabilitation Center No. 1, known as El
Altiplano, in the State of Mexico. On October 20, the initial hearing of the
federal proceedings began. His criminal responsibility must be determined
through the respective judicial rulings.

Since the presence of U.S. agents in Chihuahua became known, Morena has
questioned the conduct of the government headed by María Eugenia Campos. The
party maintains that **security cooperation with the United States must be
carried out through the legal and institutional mechanisms** established
between both countries, without allowing foreign agencies to perform
operational functions outside the Mexican federal authorities.

In that context, Montiel recalled the mobilization that Morena organized on
May 16 in the Chihuahua state capital to demand clarification of the case.
During that day, highway blockades and obstacles were reported that allegedly
prevented supporters from traveling to the rally point. The party leadership
attributed these actions to attempts to stop the protest, while the
accusations about the responsibility of state authorities remained subject to
the corresponding complaints.

"The people of Delicias were left stuck because supposed farmers had closed
the highway, when afterwards the farmers distanced themselves from an action
of this kind," Montiel said. She added that, despite the difficulties, the
participants carried on with the protest because they considered that the
foreign intervention represented a serious violation of national sovereignty.

The leader explained that, after that mobilization, Morena undertook an
information campaign to make known what happened in Chihuahua and to keep
alive the demand that all possible responsibilities be investigated.

Another of the matters pointed out by the party is cooperation with U.S.
agencies through the Torre Centinela, located in Ciudad Juárez. **Luis Ángel
Aguirre Rodríguez** , who took over the State Public Security Secretariat in
October, currently heads the agency that administers this complex.

However, it was his predecessor, Gilberto Loya Chávez, who during his tenure
spoke of allocating the 18th floor of the building to information-sharing and
collaboration activities with U.S. agencies, among them the Drug Enforcement
Administration (DEA), the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), and other
federal law enforcement agencies. The proposal raised questions about its
legal scope and the required authorization mechanisms. It has not been
established that said space was assigned to the CIA.

Referring to the investigations against PAN members, Montiel stated:

> **The first PAN member arrested for fiscal fuel theft is Ernesto Ruffo, and
> the first PAN member arrested for treason is César Jáuregui.**
>
> Ariadna Montiel Reyes, Morena national leader

She also recalled that, before his capture, the former prosecutor had publicly
defended the operation and stated that he would carry it out again.

The leader reiterated that the investigations must go all the way, without
being limited to the arrested former official, to determine who authorized,
coordinated, or facilitated the participation of foreign personnel in the
security tasks carried out in Chihuahua.
